Every vehicle that is fitted with a windscreen shall be equipped with a system for removing frost and ice from the exterior glazed surface of the windscreen.
The windscreen defrosting system shall be effective enough to ensure adequate visibility through the windscreen in cold weather.

The efficiency of the system shall be verified by determining the defrosted area of the windscreen periodically after starting, the vehicle having been kept in a cold chamber for a certain amount of time.
The requirements of points 2.1.1. and 2.1.2. shall be checked using the method set out in point 3.1.

chapeau: The following requirements shall be satisfied:
clause: 40 minutes after the start of the test period, vision area B shall be 95 % defrosted.

chapeau: The following requirements shall be satisfied:
clause: The demisting system shall be effective enough to restore visibility through the windscreen in case it is fogged up with mist.

chapeau: The following requirements shall be satisfied:
clause: Its efficiency shall be verified in accordance with the procedure described in point 3.2.

chapeau: The following requirements shall be satisfied:
clause: The following requirements shall be satisfied:

chapeau: The following requirements shall be satisfied:
clause: Vision area A shall be 90 % demisted in 10 minutes;

chapeau: The following requirements shall be satisfied:
clause: Vision area B shall be 80 % demisted in 10 minutes.
The test shall be carried out at a temperature of – 8 ± 2 °C or – 18 ± 3 °C, as selected by the manufacturer.

The test shall be carried out in a cold chamber large enough to contain the complete vehicle and equipped to maintain one of the temperatures mentioned in point 3.1.1. in the chamber throughout the test and to circulate cold air.
The cold chamber shall be maintained at or below the specified test temperature for not less than 24 hours before the start of the period during which the vehicle is exposed to cold.
Before the test, the inner and outer surfaces of the windscreen shall be thoroughly degreased by means of methylated spirit or an equivalent degreasing agent.
After drying, a solution of ammonia of not less than 3 % and not more than 10 % shall be applied.
The surface shall be allowed to dry again and then be wiped with a dry cotton cloth.
The vehicle shall be switched off and shall be kept at the test temperature for not less than 10 hours prior to commencement of the test.

Following the exposure period prescribed in point 3.1.3., an even layer of ice of 0,044 g/cm 2 shall be applied over the entire outside surface of the windscreen by means of a water spray gun working at 3,5 ± 0,2 bar operating pressure.

The spray nozzle, adjusted to full fan pattern and maximum flow, shall be held perpendicular to and at a distance of between 200 and 250 mm from the glazed surface, and so directed as to form an even layer of ice right across the windscreen from one side to the other.
Any other device by which the requirements can be satisfied shall also be permitted.
After the ice has been formed on the windscreen, the vehicle shall be kept in the cold chamber for an additional period of not less than 30 minutes and not more than 40 minutes.

After the period referred to in point 3.1.5. has elapsed, one or two observers shall enter the vehicle, subsequently the vehicle master operation control may be switched to the on position and any engine can be started, if necessary by some external means.
The test period shall commence as soon as the vehicle master control switch has been activated.

chapeau: During the final 35 minutes of the test period (or during the entire test period if the five-minute warming-up procedure is not followed) the following shall apply:
clause: The engine, if fitted, shall run at a speed not exceeding 50% of the speed corresponding to its maximum power output.

chapeau: During the final 35 minutes of the test period (or during the entire test period if the five-minute warming-up procedure is not followed) the following shall apply:
clause: However, if this is proven not to be practicable due to specific engine control strategies, for instance in the case of electric hybrid vehicles, a realistic worst case scenario shall be determined.

chapeau: During the final 35 minutes of the test period (or during the entire test period if the five-minute warming-up procedure is not followed) the following shall apply:
clause: The scenario shall take into account the engine speeds, periodical absence or complete absence of a running engine during normal driving conditions at an ambient temperature of – 8 °C or – 18 °C, whichever has been selected by the manufacturer as the designated test temperature.

chapeau: During the final 35 minutes of the test period (or during the entire test period if the five-minute warming-up procedure is not followed) the following shall apply:
clause: If the system can meet the defrosting requirements without a running engine, the engine does not have to run at all.

chapeau: During the final 35 minutes of the test period (or during the entire test period if the five-minute warming-up procedure is not followed) the following shall apply:
clause: All batteries shall be fully charged at the start of the test.

chapeau: During the final 35 minutes of the test period (or during the entire test period if the five-minute warming-up procedure is not followed) the following shall apply:
clause: However, high voltage batteries of vehicles with an electric powertrain shall be charged > 60 %.

chapeau: During the final 35 minutes of the test period (or during the entire test period if the five-minute warming-up procedure is not followed) the following shall apply:
clause: The temperature in the test chamber shall be measured at the level of the centre of the windscreen, at a point not significantly affected by heat from the vehicle under test.

chapeau: During the final 35 minutes of the test period (or during the entire test period if the five-minute warming-up procedure is not followed) the following shall apply:
clause: The horizontal component of the speed of the air cooling the chamber, measured immediately prior to the test, in the median plane of the vehicle at a point 300 mm forward of the base of the windscreen and at a level half-way between the base and the top of the windscreen, shall be as low as possible and in any event less than 8 km/h.

chapeau: During the final 35 minutes of the test period (or during the entire test period if the five-minute warming-up procedure is not followed) the following shall apply:
clause: If fitted, the engine bonnet, roof, all doors, windows and vents, except the intakes and outlets of the heating and ventilating system, shall be closed;

chapeau: During the final 35 minutes of the test period (or during the entire test period if the five-minute warming-up procedure is not followed) the following shall apply:
clause: The vehicle's defrosting system controls shall be set as recommended by the vehicle manufacturer for the test temperature.

chapeau: During the final 35 minutes of the test period (or during the entire test period if the five-minute warming-up procedure is not followed) the following shall apply:
clause: The windscreen wipers may be used during the test, but this shall be done without any manual assistance apart from the operation of any controls in the interior of the vehicle.

chapeau: During the final 35 minutes of the test period (or during the entire test period if the five-minute warming-up procedure is not followed) the following shall apply:
clause: The observer(s) shall outline the defrosted area on the inside surface of the windscreen, at five-minute intervals from the start of the test period.

chapeau: During the final 35 minutes of the test period (or during the entire test period if the five-minute warming-up procedure is not followed) the following shall apply:
clause: Before the test, the inside and outer surfaces of the windscreen shall be thoroughly degreased by means of methylated spirit, or an equivalent degreasing agent.
